title: Noise-floor sweep standup notes
content:
Attendees: Priya (note), Evan, Marco, Yasmin, Jordan (remotely)

Purpose: quick sync to capture the noise-floor sweep results, outstanding repro steps for the throughput regression seen on 11/14, and decide next week’s focused runs. Keep this lightweight — we need runnable, shareable steps for SRE and QA.

Summary of what we saw (quick bullets):
- Baseline (pre-11/10) p95 for 256-token seq: ~28 ms; current p95: ~52–58 ms under identical shadow load.
- Throughput drop: nominal QPS at target 120 dropped to ~106 (12% loss) on NVidia A10-like nodes when sequence length increases to 512 tokens.
- p99 spikes align with small microbursts in client arrival pattern; but those microbursts do not fully explain sustained p95 increase.
- KV cache hit rate measured during runs: 72% baseline vs 69% current — small but may amplify under batching heuristics.
- Observed increase in CPU time on sidecar process (c++ shard) during the warmup phase — possible GC or thread contention.

Repro attempts to date (what worked / didn’t):
- Re-ran our nightly shadow harness (bench-harness:v2) with identical seed traffic — reproduced on 3/3 runs.
- Disabled prefix caching in an isolated run -> p95 dropped back to ~31 ms. Suggests caching path interacts with new kernel selection. (See run id: sweep-20241119-03)
- Reverted PR 768 (kernel selection tweak) in a canary -> p95 improved but throughput jitter increased. Reversion was partial (didn’t revert sidecar threading changes).
- Local single-node repro (docker dev) DOES NOT reproduce — problem only visible at fleet scale or with load shaping that produces inter-arrival variability.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel selection change (PR 768) chooses a slightly different matmul kernel that raises tail latency for medium sequences when cache hits are present. (evidence: revert improved p95)
2) Sidecar thread contention due to increased CPU on warmup path causes elevated queuing for batches. (evidence: CPU spike on sidecar)
3) Batching heuristic + slightly lower KV hit rate produce more variable batch sizes which bump serialization overhead. (evidence: hit rate delta + increased batch size variance in traces)

Key traces & artifacts to inspect:
- Trace samples: trace-20241119-03-{a,b,c} (attached in Slack thread)
- Flame graphs: sidecar-warmup-flame-11-19.svg (in PR artifacts)
- Benchmark logs: /bench/artifacts/sweep-20241119-03/*.log
- Live QPS replay script: scripts/replay_with_jitter.sh (adds exponential jitter to inter-arrival)

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Evan: build an A/B harness that toggles kernel picker only (no threading changes), run 6x with jittered arrivals; produce p95/p99 table. ETA: 2024-11-22.
- Marco: capture and diff sidecar flame graphs for warmup path between baseline and current; instrument with nanoslice timer around thread pool dequeue. ETA: 2024-11-24.
- Yasmin: run KV cache instrumentation (increase logging of eviction/hit paths) on a small fleet (10 nodes) and correlate with batch size histogram. ETA: 2024-11-23.
- Priya: orchestrate a mid-week smoke run with SRE to reproduce at 250 QPS for 30m using production traffic profile; prepare rollback checklist. ETA: 2024-11-25.

Short runnable checklist for anyone who wants to reproduce locally (notes + commands):
1) pull bench harness: git checkout bench-harness:v2 (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness)
2) run the jittered replay: ./scripts/replay_with_jitter.sh --qps 120 --duration 600 --seed 42 --dest $TEST_CLUSTER
3) enable detailed trace sampling: POST /_admin/trace-config {"rate":0.1, "samples":50}
4) collect KV metrics: curl $METRIC_ENDPOINT/?tag=kvcache&window=60s > kv.log
5) collect sidecar flame: curl $SIDECAR/pulse > flame.json; convert with flameview

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does disabling prefix cache flip latency back — is the cache validation path more expensive post-PR? (need to inspect cache lock hold times)
- Is there a coupling between selected matmul kernel and memory access pattern that causes increased contention on shared buffers?
- How much of observed p99 spikes are client-side arrival variability vs server-side serialization? Need tighter client-side shaping to isolate.

Notes to self (quick):
- If A/B with kernel-only toggle reproduces, file a hotfix branch: perf/hotfix/kernel-rollback-20241122.
- Keep any production toggles limited to 5% traffic until we have >10 runs.
- Add a small synthetic test in CI that runs 512-token mixed load for 5 minutes to catch regressions early. (low-cost smoke)

Decision made in meeting: prioritize kernel-picker A/B (Evan) and sidecar flame analysis (Marco). If kernel-picker A/B is sufficient (i.e., shows regression), we will ship a targeted rollback and re-run canary.

Follow-ups scheduled: quick readout Wed 11/22 09:30 PST (15 min). Longer retro on Fri 11/24 11:00 PST (30 min) to close actions and decide on CI change.

Misc references / links:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01PERF123/p1700000000000000
- Jira PERF-4123 (throughput regression investigation)
- PR 768 discussion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/768

End of notes.

(rough / iterative — will tidy once A/B runs done)
